newsitem.title: JAPAN: No tax break for Japan aluminium alloy import-MITI.
newsitem.headline: No tax break for Japan aluminium alloy import-MITI.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry decided not to include aluminium alloy among items subject to a tax-break scheme for promoting imports, a MITI official said on Wednesday.
Aluminium alloy was to become eligible for the tax break starting in the fiscal year beginning April 1997 after tariffs on alloy imports were abolished in April 1995.
The ministry determined, however, that aluminium alloy should be considered an internationally traded commodity, which is among the items excluded from the tax-break programme, the official said.

The programme allows companies which increase their purchases of an imported item to claim a tax deduction on the portion of the purchases that exceeds the previous year's level, with a ceiling of 15 percent for small businesses and 10 percent for other firms. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk (81-3 3432 6179)
